title: Row Row Row Your Boat
about: This is one of the best known children's songs in the English-speaking world. Eliphalet Oram Lyte published the tune we sing today in 1881, in The Franklin Square Song Collection. It walks up the first five notes of the scale, then tumbles down a whole octave.
funFact: The song is a round: a second voice starts the same tune two bars later, and the two parts fit together.

practice.text: Play the right hand alone, slowly, and let the song wait for each note.
Play bars 5 to 8 with the right hand alone, where the tune runs down.
Put both hands together. The left hand only holds a long low note.
Play the whole song with both hands at full speed.

tips.text: Each finger has its own key here: thumb on C, little finger on G.
The G lasts the whole bar, so count all six beats before you move.
Each note here lasts three beats, so count to three on every key.

tricky.text: Move the hand up during the long G, so the little finger lands on the high C.
Hold E with finger 2, then C with the thumb, for three beats each. Keep the hand still.
The little finger finds G again, and the tune walks down: 5, 4, 3, 2.

practice.text: Play the left hand alone, and press the three notes of each chord together.
Play the left hand of the second half, where a bass note comes before each chord.
Join the hands on the first eight bars, slowly.
Play the whole song with both hands at full speed.

tips.text: The chord moves down one key: only the little finger leaves C for B.
The bass note falls on beat one, and the notes above it on beat four.
Let the falling notes get a little softer, like a boat drifting away.

tricky.text: Move the right hand up during the long G, so the little finger lands on the high C.
The high C comes back. Move the right hand up during the long G of bar 12.
In the left hand, the little finger slides from C to B and the third finger from E to D.

practice.text: Play the Alberti bass alone until it rolls by itself: low, high, middle, high.
Play the tune in the left hand alone, from bar 9.
Join the hands on the first eight bars, slowly.
Play the whole song with both hands at three quarters speed.
Now play it at full speed, with the pedal.

tips.text: Keep the Alberti bass soft, so the tune sings above it.
Lift the pedal and press it again on beats one and four.
The tune moves to the left hand. Play it louder than the right hand's broken chords.

tricky.text: Move the right hand up during the long G, so the little finger is ready on the high C.
Both hands change jobs here: the left hand takes the tune, and the right hand takes the chords.
Your left thumb reaches up to middle C, then the hand walks down with 2, 3 and 5.

practice.text: Play the right hand's chords alone, and let the little finger sing the tune.
Play the left hand alone from bar 9, where it starts the round.
Join the hands on the round, slowly, and listen for the two voices.
Play the whole song with both hands at three quarters speed.
Now play it at full speed, and make the last chord ring.

tips.text: Play the top note of each chord a little louder than the others.
The left hand starts the round alone. The right hand waits two bars.
Each hand plays the whole tune. Let both voices be heard.

tricky.text: Spread the right hand over a whole octave for the last chord: C, E, G and C.
The right hand ends the round alone. Lift it after the D, ready for the last chord.
Lift the hand off the chord of bar 4, and land with the little finger on the high C.
